(p-461) Surah Fatir

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾. Al-Fatr (splitting) means cleaving something open so that it is made manifest for what is beautiful. It is said: "fatara nab al-naqah" when the tooth of the she-camel emerges, and "fatara damahu" when he let out his blood.

Ibn Abbas said: "I did not know what Fatir of the heavens and the earth meant until two Bedouin men came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said: 'Ana fatartuha,' i.e., I initiated it."

Regarding its interpretation here there are two views:

First: the Creator of the heavens and the earth. This was said by Qatadah, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil.

Second: that He split them open for what descends from them and what ascends within them.

﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾. Regarding this there are two views:

First: messengers to the prophets. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: messengers to the servants, as mercy or as punishment. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿Possessors of wings, two, three, or four﴾. Qatadah said: some of them have two wings, some three, and some four.

Al-mathna, al-thulath and al-ruba' mean that two, three, or four are repeated in it.

(p-462) ﴿He adds to creation what He wills﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: that it is beauty of voice. This was said by al-Zuhri and Ibn Jurayj.

Second: that it is curly hair. This was related by al-Naqqash.

Third: He adds to the wings of the angels what He wills. This was said by al-Hasan.

It may also be understood, as a fourth possibility, that it is intellect and discernment.

It may also be understood, as a fifth possibility, that it is knowledge and crafts.

The meaning according to these two interpretations is: just as He adds to creation what He wills, so He adds to the wings of the angels what He wills.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verses 2–6:

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to the people, none can withhold it﴾. Regarding this there are seven interpretations:

First: [it is] of goodness (khayr). This is related from Qatadah.

Second: [it is] of rain (matar). This is related from al-Suddi.

Third: [it is] of repentance (tawbah). This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Fourth: [it is] of revelation (wahy). This is related from al-Hasan.

Fifth: [it is] of provision (rizq), and this is transmitted from the Prophet's Companions (ma'thur).

(p-463) Sixth: [it is] of well-being (ʿafiyah). This is related from al-Kalbi.

Seventh: [it is] of supplication (duʿa'). This is related from al-Dahhak.

And it may admit an eighth: [it is] of divine success (tawfiq) and guidance (hidayah).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verses 7–8:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good...﴾ On this there are four opinions:

The first: They are the Jews, the Christians and the Magians. This was said by Abu Qilabah, and the "evil of his deed" would be his opposition to the Messenger.

The second: They are the Kharijites. It was transmitted by Amr ibn al-Qasim, and the "evil of his deed" would be distorting the interpretation (ta'wil).

The third: It is Satan. This was said by al-Hasan, and the "evil of his deed" would be misleading (al-ighwa').

The fourth: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh. This was said by al-Kalbi, and the "evil of their deed" would be shirk (associating partners with God).

It was also said that it was revealed concerning al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and others said it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Regarding His saying ﴿so that he sees it as good﴾ there are two meanings:

One of them: "correct" (sawaban). This was said by al-Kalbi.

The second: "beautiful" (jamilan).

In the speech there is an omitted element (mahdhuf), on which opinions differ in three ways:

The first: The omitted part is: "Then indeed he will be filled with regret over it on the Day of Resurrection." This was said by Ibn Isa.

The second: The omitted part is: "Is he like one who believes and does righteous deeds? They are not equal." This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The third: The omitted part is: "Is he like one who does good and evil?"

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verse 9–11:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Whoever desires honour—then to Allah belongs all honour﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: By "honour" is meant protection (al-mana'ah), so that one seeks strength through obedience to Allah, Most High. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: "Knowledge of whom honour belongs to"; so to Allah belongs all honour.

It is said that the occasion of revelation of this verse is what al-Hasan related: that the polytheists worshipped idols so that they would grant them honour, as Allah, Most High, described them in His saying: ﴿And they have taken other than Allah as gods so that they might be for them a source of honour﴾. Then Allah, Most High, revealed: ﴿Whoever desires honour—then to Allah belongs all honour﴾.

﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: that it is monotheism (al-tawhid). This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

The second: the praise of the righteous believers on earth, which the drawn-near angels carry up. This was related by al-Naqqash.

﴿And righteous deeds raise it up﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: that it is the performance of the obligatory duties (al-fara'id).

The second: that it is the doing of all acts of nearness (al-qurab) to Allah.

Concerning His saying ﴿raises it up﴾ there are three opinions:

The first: that righteous deed is raised up by the good word. This was said by al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Sallam.

The second: that righteous deed raises up the good word. This was said by al-Dahhak and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The third: that deed is raised up by Allah along with its doer. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi.

﴿And those who plot evil deeds﴾, meaning: those who commit shirk in the world.

(p-465) ﴿For them is a severe punishment﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter.

﴿And the plotting of those—it will perish﴾. Concerning this there are three aspects:

The first: it will be corrupted before Allah, Most High. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

The second: it will be void. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: it will be destroyed, and al-bawar (ruin) is destruction. This was said by Qutrub.

Concerning who is meant by "those": there are two opinions:

One: the people of shirk.

The second: the people of usury (al-riba). This was said by Mujahid.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾, meaning Adam.

﴿Then from a drop of semen﴾, meaning his offspring.

﴿Then He made you into pairs﴾. Concerning this there are two aspects:

One: kinds (asnaf). This was said by al-Kalbi.

The second: males and females. The one that has with it another of its kind is a pair (zawj), and two are a pair (zawjan). Allah, Most High, said: ﴿And that He created the two kinds, the male and the female﴾ [al-Najm: 45]. Qatadah interpreted His saying, Most High, ﴿Then He made you into pairs﴾ as meaning: some of you were married to others.

﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾, meaning: by His command.

﴿Nor is one granted long life or has any of his life shortened﴾, to the end of the verse.

Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: what We extend of the lifespan of one who is granted long life until he becomes decrepit (haram); and no one's life is shortened until he dies as a child, except that it is in a Book.

The second: whoever is granted long life, when Allah has decreed the term of his appointed time, whatever is decreased from it by the days that have passed over him is recorded in a Book with Allah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is a scroll in which Allah wrote his term at its beginning, then wrote at its bottom: "a day such-and-such passed, and a day such-and-such," until he reaches his term. Abu Malik and al-Sha'bi said the same.

Concerning the lifespan of the one granted long life there are three opinions:

The first: sixty years. This was said by al-Hasan.

The second: forty years.

The third: eighteen years. This was said by Abu Ghalib.

﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾, i.e., effortless.

It may bear two meanings:

One: that the recording of that is easy for Allah.

The second: that the increase in the life of one granted long life and the decrease in the life of another is easy in the sight of Allah, Most High.

For al-Kalbi there is a third: that the preservation of that without a Book is easy for Allah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verse 12–14:

﴿And the two seas are not alike﴾ (wa-ma yastawi al-bahran) admits of two meanings:

The first: that they are not alike in themselves.

The second: in the benefits people derive from them.

﴿This one is sweet and fresh﴾ (ʿadhbun furat). Al-furat is the same as al-ʿadhb (sweet), and he mentioned it for emphasis, given the difference in the two words, as one says "this is good and beautiful" (hadha hasanun jamil).

﴿Pleasant to drink, its water﴾ (sa'igh sharabuhu), i.e., its water.

﴿And this one is salty and bitter﴾ (wa-hadha milhun ujaj), i.e., bitter, taken from ajjat al-nar (the blaze of fire), as if it burns because of the intensity of its bitterness. The poet said:

؎ A pearl in the right hand, which he brought out, reaching from the depth of a sea that is salty and bitter

(p-467) ﴿And from each of them you eat fresh flesh﴾, meaning the flesh of fish, eaten from both seas.

﴿And you extract ornaments which you wear﴾. Pearls and coral are extracted from the salt water, and the intended meaning is one of them, even though the speech is joined to both of them.

It was also said: rather, it is taken from both of them, because in the sea there are sweet springs, and between them pearls emerge at the mingling; and it was said it comes from the rain of the sky.

Then He said: ﴿you wear them﴾, although women wear them rather than men, because their beauty returns to all of them.

﴿And you see the ships therein cleaving [the water]﴾ (mawakhir). In it there are five aspects:

The first: advancing and retreating with one wind, said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: laden, said by al-Hasan.

The poet said:

؎ You see them, when they go along heavy, as if they were ships cleaving or camels loaded with burdens

The third: crosswise, said by Abu Wa'il.

The fourth: sailing (jawari), said by Ibn Qutaybah.

The fifth: plowing the water, i.e., cutting it as they run, said by ʿAli ibn ʿIsa.

﴿That you may seek of His bounty﴾. Mujahid said: trade by ship.

It may also admit another meaning: what is extracted from its ornaments and what is hunted of fish.

﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [in it are two aspects]:

The first: for what He has given you of His blessings.

The second: for what He has given you of His bounty.

And it may admit a third: for what He has rescued you from its terror.

Qutrub said: al-harur is the heat, and al-zill (الظِّلّ) is the coolness.

The second: it is negating the equality of one of them with the other.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verse 27–28:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors?﴾ In it there is an omitted implied element, its estimated form being "varying in their colors, their tastes, and their scents." He restricted the mention to color because it is the most apparent of them. ﴿And of the mountains are streaks, white and red of varying shades, and extremely dark black.﴾ In it there are two views:

The first: that the judad (streaks) are pieces, derived from "jaddadtu al-shay'" (I cut the thing) when you cut it. This was related by Ibn Bahr.

The second: that they are the lines (strata), whose singular is jaddah, like muddah and mudad (period and periods). From this is the saying of Zuhayr:

"As if he were a dark-cheeked one with streaks, lean, who grazes naked after the summer."

﴿White and red, of varying colors, and extremely dark black.﴾ The ghirbib (extremely dark) is that which is intensely black, whose color is like the color of the crow (ghurab).

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah dislikes the old man who is ghirbib," meaning the one who dyes (his hair) with black. Imru' al-Qays said:

"The eye is eager, the hand is swimming, and the leg is burning, and the face is ghirbib."

It has also been said that there is inversion and transposition in it, and its estimated form is "black, extremely dark (ghara'ib)."

Regarding what is meant by "extremely dark black" there are three views:

The first: the black mountains; this was said by al-Suddi.

The second: the black tracts of land (taraif); this was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: the black valleys; this was said by Qatadah.

﴿And of mankind, and beasts, and cattle, their colors are likewise varying.﴾ In it there are two views:

The first: "Likewise, their colors vary: white, red and black."

The second: by His saying "likewise" He means: just as the colors of the fruits, the mountains, the people, the beasts and the cattle vary, so too the states of the servants vary in fear (of Allah).

Then He resumed, saying: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah.﴾ By "those of knowledge" He means those who fear.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: Whoever does not fear Allah is not a scholar.

Ibn Mas'ud said: The God-fearing are masters, and the scholars are leaders.

It has also been said: the opening of the Zabur is wisdom, which is the fear of Allah.

(p-472) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They hope for a commerce that will never perish﴾, meaning Paradise. There are two interpretations of this:

The first: it will never decay. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: it will never go unsold (lose its market). This was said by Ali ibn Isa. The first is more fitting, due to the saying of the poet:

"O Messenger of the Sovereign, indeed my tongue is a mender; whatever I tear apart, I (then) am ruined (bur)."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That He may pay them their rewards﴾, meaning the reward of their deeds.

﴿And increase them of His bounty﴾. Regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first: their graves will be widened for them. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: He will grant them intercession on behalf of those who did them good in the world. This was said by Abu Wa'il.

The third: He will multiply their good deeds for them. This is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) (transmitted).

The fourth: forgiveness of much and appreciation of little. This was said by some of the later scholars.

It may also admit a fifth: He will pay them their rewards for performing acts of obedience and increase them of His bounty for avoiding acts of disobedience. ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving﴾ of sins,

﴿Appreciative﴾ of obedience.

Describing Him as "Appreciative" is metaphorical; its meaning is that He repays good with good in the manner of one who appreciates, since He rewards a small deed with many times its worth.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (*al-Nukat wa al-'Uyun*) on Surah 35, verses 31–32:

﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾. In this there are two views:

The first: the Book is the Qur'an, and the meaning of inheritance (*al-irth*) is the transfer of the ruling to them.

The second: the inheritance of the Book is belief in the earlier scriptures, because the real meaning of inheritance is the transfer of a thing from one people to another.

(p-٤٧٣) Regarding ﴿those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ there are three opinions:

The first: they are the Prophets. This was related by Ibn 'Isa.

The second: they are the Children of Israel, based on the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 33], and so on.

This was stated by Ibn Bahr.

The third: they are the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ). This was stated by al-Kalbi.

﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate﴾. In this there are two views:

The first: the words ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ are a new statement that does not refer back to the chosen ones. This is the view of those who interpreted the chosen ones as the Prophets, so that those other than them become three categories, as he explained.

The second: it refers back to the detailed states of those whom We have chosen. The meaning of *al-istifa'* (choosing) is selection. This is the view of those who interpreted the chosen ones as other than the Prophets, and so made them three categories.

As for the one who wrongs himself here, there are five views:

The first: they are the people of minor sins from this Ummah. Shahr ibn Hawshab related that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Our foremost is foremost, our moderate one is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven."

The second: they are the people of major sins and the companions of the left hand (*al-mash'amah*). This was stated by al-Suddi.

The third: they are the hypocrites, and they are excluded.

The fourth: they are the People of the Book. This was stated by al-Hasan.

The fifth: he is the one who denies (the truth). This was stated by Mujahid.

As for the moderate one, there are four opinions:

The first: he is the one who is intermediate in acts of obedience. This is the meaning of the hadith of Abu al-Darda'. Ibrahim related from Abu Salih, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited this verse and said: "As for the foremost, he will enter Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate one, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained for a long period, then Allah will overlook him."

(p-٤٧٤) The second: they are the companions of the right hand (*ashab al-yamin*). This was stated by al-Suddi.

The third: they are the people of minor sins. This is a later view.

The fourth: they are those who followed the Sunnah (*sunan*) of the Prophet (ﷺ) after him. This was stated by al-Hasan.

﴿And among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾. In this there are four opinions:

The first: they are those brought near (*al-muqarrabun*). This was stated by Mujahid.

The second: they are those who increase in obedience to Allah, the Exalted. This is related on authority (*ma'thur*).

The third: they are the people of the highest rank in acts of obedience. This was stated by 'Ali ibn 'Isa.

The fourth: he is the one who died during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to whom he bore witness of Paradise.

'Uqbah ibn Suhban related that he said: "I asked 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) about this verse, and she said: 'All of them are from the people of Paradise. The foremost is the one who died during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to whom he bore witness of life and provision. The moderate one is the one who followed his footsteps until he joined him. The one who wrongs himself is like me and like you, and those who follow us.'"

(p-475) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to God, who has removed from us all sorrow."﴾ On this there are nine interpretations:

First: It is the fear of Hellfire. Said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

Second: It is the sorrow of death. Said by ʿAtiyyah.

Third: It is the toil of this world and its worries. Said by Qatadah.

Fourth: It is the sorrow of obligation (al-minnah). Said by Samurah.

Fifth: It is the sorrow of the wrongdoer at what he witnesses of his own evil state. Said by Ibn Zayd.

Sixth: It is hunger. Related by al-Naqqash.

Seventh: It is fear of the ruler. Related by al-Kalbi.

Eighth: It is the pursuit of livelihood. Related by al-Farra'.

Ninth: It is the sorrow of food, and this is transmitted from the Prophet's companions (ma'thur).

It may also admit a tenth: that it is the sorrow of hatred and envy, because the people of Paradise are bound together in affection; they do not hate one another nor envy one another.

Regarding the time of their saying this, there are two views:

One: At the giving of their books in their right hands, for that is the first of the glad tidings of safety, so they will say at that moment: ﴿Praise be to God, who has removed from us all sorrow.﴾

Two: After entering Paradise. Said by al-Kalbi, and this is closer to the truth, since the reward is settled and they are freed from the terrors of the Resurrection; so they will say this in thanks upon feeling secure.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence by His bounty.﴾ That is, the abode of residence (al-iqamah), which is Paradise.

Regarding the difference between al-muqamah with a ḍammah and with a fatḥah, there are two views:

One: With a ḍammah it means the abode of residence, and with a fatḥah it means the place of residence.

Two: With a ḍammah it means the assembly in which people gather for conversation.

Two: Pain (wajaʿ). Said by Qatadah.

﴿Nor does weariness touch us therein﴾ (lughub). On this there are two views:

(p-476) One: It is exhaustion (al-ʿanaʾ). Said by Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari.

Two: It is fatigue (al-iʿyaʾ). Said by Qutrub and Ibn ʿIsa.

It may also admit a tenth: that it is the sorrow of hatred and envy, because the people of Paradise are bound together in affection; they do not hate one another nor envy one another.

Regarding the time of their saying this, there are two views:

One: At the giving of their books in their right hands, for that is the first of the glad tidings of safety, so they will say at that moment: ﴿Praise be to God, who has removed from us all sorrow.﴾

Two: After entering Paradise. Said by al-Kalbi, and this is closer to the truth, since the reward is settled and they are freed from the terrors of the Resurrection; so they will say this in thanks upon feeling secure.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence by His bounty.﴾ That is, the abode of residence (al-iqamah), which is Paradise.

Regarding the difference between al-muqamah with a ḍammah and with a fatḥah, there are two views:

One: With a ḍammah it means the abode of residence, and with a fatḥah it means the place of residence.

Two: With a ḍammah it means the assembly in which people gather for conversation.

﴿No fatigue touches us therein﴾ (nasab). On this there are two views:

One: Toil (taʿab). Said by Ibn ʿIsa.

Two: Pain (wajaʿ). Said by Qatadah.

﴿Nor does weariness touch us therein﴾ (lughub). On this there are two views:

(p-476) One: It is exhaustion (al-ʿanaʾ). Said by Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari.

Two: It is fatigue (al-iʿyaʾ). Said by Qutrub and Ibn ʿIsa.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verses 36–37:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And they will cry out therein﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: "And they will cry for help therein. ﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do﴾," meaning: we will believe instead of disbelieving, and obey instead of disobeying.

﴿Did We not give you lives long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾ Regarding this there are five interpretations:

The first: it is the attainment of maturity (bulugh, reaching the age of legal responsibility). This was said by al-Hasan, because it is the first time of being mindful.

The second: eighteen years.

The third: forty years. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Masruq.

The fourth: sixty years. This was said by Ali ibn Abi Talib, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

The fifth: seventy years, because it is the last time of being mindful, and after it comes decrepitude.

Abu Hurayrah narrated that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has left no excuse for a servant whose term He has delayed until he reached sixty or seventy years."

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And the warner came to you﴾. Regarding this there are four sayings:

The first: Muhammad (ﷺ). This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: white hair (grey hair, al-shayb). This was related by al-Farra' and al-Tabari.

The third: fever.

The fourth: the death of family and relatives.

And it may be a fifth: that it is the perfection of reason (kamal al-aql).

"Taste [it]" (﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾) admits two meanings:

First: the anguish of regret.

Second: the punishment of Hell.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾. Qatadah said: "Successors after successors, generation after generation." The khalaf (successor) is the one who comes after the one who preceded him. For this reason, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was addressed as "O successor of Allah," and he said: "I am not the successor of Allah, but I am the successor of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I am content with that."

Some said, after the predecessors (al-salaf): one is only made a successor (yustakhlaf) when he is absent or dies, and Allah, Exalted, neither is absent nor dies.

﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, i.e., upon him is the punishment for his disbelief.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah?﴾ In it there are two meanings:

First: your partners in the wealth, of which you assigned to them a portion, [namely] the idols.

Second: those whom you associated with Him in worship.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verses 40–41:

﴿Show me what they have created from the earth.﴾ Said by al-Suddi, meaning: "in the earth."

﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ Until they became partners in creating them.

﴿Or have We given them a Book, so that they stand upon clear proof from it?﴾ In this there are three aspects:

The first: "Or have We sent down to them a Book stating that God, exalted is He, has partners from among the angels and the idols, and that they hold fast to it." This is the view of Ibn Ziyad.

(p-478) The second: "Or have We sent down to them a Book stating that God will not punish them for their disbelief, so that they feel secure in it." This is the meaning of the statement of al-Kalbi.

﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion.﴾ In this there are two aspects:

The first: They promised them that the angels would intercede.

The second: They promised them that they would be victorious over them.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verse 42–43:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And they swore by Allah with the utmost of their oaths﴾. They are the Quraysh, who swore before Allah Most High sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), when news reached them that the People of the Book had denied their messengers. So they cursed whoever among them had denied his prophet, and they swore an oath by Allah, whose name is exalted.

﴿Indeed, if a warner (nadhir) came to them﴾, that is, a prophet.

﴿They would surely be better guided than any (other) of the nations﴾, meaning than those among the People of the Book who denied the messengers.

﴿But when a warner did come to them﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿It increased them in nothing but aversion﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: aversion from the Messenger.

The second: aversion from the truth.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Arrogance in the land﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: arrogance toward the worship of Allah. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: arrogance through the disobedience of Allah. This is a later opinion.

﴿And evil plotting﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: associating partners with Allah. This was said by Yahya.

(p-479) The second: that it is plotting against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his religion, as the Most High said: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30], and so on.

﴿But evil plotting does not encompass its own people except (them)﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: this was said by al-Kalbi, that "yahiq" means "yuhit" (encompasses).

The second: this was said by Qutrub, that "yahiq" means "yanzil" (descends). He recited the poet's verse:

"They warded off death, and the (arm's) length was made to recede, after it had nearly descended."

He said: so that returned upon them through their being killed on the Day of Badr.

﴿So do they await anything but the way (sunnah) of the former peoples?﴾, meaning the way of Allah concerning the former peoples. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: the descent of punishment upon them when they persist in denial.

The second: repentance will not be accepted from them when the punishment descends.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 35, verses 44–45:

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿If Allah were to seize mankind for what they have earned﴾ meaning, for sins.

﴿He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature﴾. Yahya ibn Sallam said: by withholding rain from them. Regarding this there are three opinions:

The first: it means all living creatures, of whatever crawls and walks. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud. Qatadah said: and He did this at the time of Nuh (peace be upon him).

The second: [it refers to] jinn and humans only, and not others, because they are both held accountable through reason. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The third: [it refers to] mankind alone. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

(p-480) ﴿but He defers them until an appointed term﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One of them: the appointed term is that which He promised them in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). This was said by Muqatil.

The second: until the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Yahya.

﴿So when their term comes﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One of them: the descent of the punishment.

The second: the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever, of His servants, All-Seeing﴾. This admits of two meanings:

One of them: All-Seeing of their term.

The second: All-Seeing of their deeds. And Allah knows best.
